first_prompt: Formally prove example 285 as elegantly and efficiently as possible

commits.summary: jvmcontract: a property check gives an interface parameter an implementation, reads accessors and Strings, and runs a HashMap model, for example 285 (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 285 (CVE-2023-34055, Spring Boot's WebMvcTags.method(HttpServletRequest)) had every proof task refused before any proof (VF-027): a property check made no input of an interface type, its expressions had no String terms and read no interface, the fix resolves the method through a HashMap that HttpMethod's class initializer fills, and the gap scan of the fixed release ran into its two-minute limit. The verifier is extended so that the frozen claim is decided as stated, on the released JARs, with no wrapper and no narrower subject.

What changed in lib/:
- A parameter of an interface type is given an implementation (src/given.rs): a generated class that answers each accessor the target may call (an abstract method of no parameters returning an integer, a boolean or a String) with one value, the same on every call. It is an object made by its constructor, so the accessors' values are the harness's symbolic inputs; the domain line and the statement say what that covers, a witness reads `method(request=HttpServletRequest{getMethod()="TRACE"})`, and the interpreter and a JVM replay the same class file. A method it doesn't answer is a named gap, never passed over.
- A property's expressions read an interface's object through its accessors and a String by content: `result.getKey().equals("method")`, `request.getMethod() != null` (src/harness/expr.rs). A property check now takes a String inside any object it makes, as the regression check does.
- The own checker runs a model of java.util.HashMap (lib/models/java/util/HashMap.java: HashMap(), HashMap(int), put, get, containsKey, size, isEmpty), models String.hashCode, runs a modelled String method whatever class the call names (Object.equals, CharSequence.length), and reproduces Objects.requireNonNull and Pattern.compile of a constant regular expression of a plain form the JDK always compiles. Each has an evidence record in values::OPERATIONS, sampled by cases that must agree on a JVM, in the interpreter and in the checker; 28 operations outside the records are checked to stay named gaps.
- The gap scan follows a virtual or interface call into the classes of the objects it has seen made, not every class below the call's owner, classifies such a call once it has seen them all, and decides a class initializer in one memoized walk. The scan of example 285's fixed release went from over two minutes (its limit) to 0.04 s, and HttpMethod's initializer is no longer judged outside the fragment for what an unrelated Map of the class path does.
- The contract library's contract for HashMap.<init>(int) is taken out with its records: the call is the model's, no gap.

Verified inline: the default run, python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py run, 34 of 34 (cargo test and every Python suite), which includes the new lib/tests/interface_parameters.rs (a label bounded through an enum's map proved, the raw label and a claim that forgets a verb refuted on a JVM, what an implementation doesn't answer refused by name, the scan's dispatch), a unit test of the expression terms, and the values corpus, where every new case (String.hashCode, the map's seven calls over String and null keys and two keys of one hash, requireNonNull, Pattern.compile) gives the JVM's outcome in the interpreter and in the checker. On the cached JARs of example 285 and a debug build, the frozen assertion under --nullable request, --gaps strict and --max-array-length 8 was refuted on Spring Boot 2.7.17 (witness HttpServletRequest{getMethod()=""}, run on a JVM), established on 2.7.18 in 0.1 s, and refuted on the mutant; dropping a name from the assertion is refuted on 2.7.18, so the proof is not vacuous. Those inline runs are no receipts, and JBMC was not run.

Verification pending: jobs 20261115-173146-example-285-vulnerable-security-the-boun, 20261115-173146-example-285-fixed-security-the-bounded-m and 20261115-173146-example-285-mutant-security-the-bounded (the three tasks' ordinary attempts through build.py, the gap packets' closure test: the unchanged claim 196346d46d4d81fb on the same artifacts), 20261115-173209-conformance-corpus-under-jbmc-auto-and-a (the conformance corpus's proof tier, where JBMC runs the HashMap model) and 20261115-173209-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c (the object comparisons' proof tier, since the harness reads fields through a new emitter). Example 285's sidecar keeps its blockers until the receipts decide; its notes say what is queued. The preservation task is still blocked on the two dependency closures, which is next.

commits.summary: jvmcontract: a regression check runs each version on its own dependency closure and over an interface parameter, for example 285's preservation (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 285's preservation task (Spring Boot 2.7.17 against 2.7.18, WebMvcTags.method(HttpServletRequest), the known-method-labels-preserved claim) was not executed: the two releases have dependency closures of other bytes, and jvmcontract's equivalence took one class path for both (VF-027's verifier-interface:two-dependency-closures). Behind that refusal a regression check also made no input of an interface type and compared two results of an interface type by Objects.equals, which says nothing about objects of two relocated classes. The regression check is extended so that the frozen claim is decided as stated, each release on its own pinned closure.

What changed in lib/:
- equivalence --before-classpath gives the previous version a dependency closure of its own (relocate::with_closure). Its build is relocated under before/ as always, and with it every class of its closure that the build names, directly or through the closure's classes in turn (a class entry, a descriptor or a generic signature of the constant pool), so both versions run in one program, each on its own libraries. A class only the new closure has is renamed in the previous version's references too, to a class that does not exist, so the previous version never runs on the new version's. Nothing is shared between two closures, JDK classes apart. Without the option both versions run on --classpath, as before.
- A parameter of an interface type is given an implementation in a regression check as in a property check (src/given.rs): one generated class per version, answering the accessors either version may call, the two objects made from the same values. A given implementation's fields are final, so nothing of it is compared after the calls.
- A result of an interface type that the previous version has its own copy of is compared through the interface's accessors, a String by content, two nulls agreeing; the statement says so. An interface with an abstract method that is no accessor, or with none, is refused by name (given::unread).
- --unchanged-unless reads a given object as Java does, on the new version's (request != null && !request.getMethod().equals("GET")). An input on which the expression throws is not among those the change is meant for, so the versions are compared on it. Such an expression beside an object made by its constructor is refused by name.
- JBMC is given neither a given implementation nor a closure of the previous version's own: --engine jbmc and --confirm are refused by name, as are --before-target, --before-arguments, --results-agree-when and a correspondence over an interface parameter.

examples/tools/targets/runtime.py passes the previous revision's dependencies as --before-classpath when the pair's closures differ, where it refused the pair before; a pair with one closure of the same bytes is run as before.

Verified by: lib/tests/interface_regression.rs (new, tool tier, a fixture of two library closures): a fix over an interface parameter proved preserved outside its declared change, refuted with no change declared, on a version that changes a known input and on one that reads a second accessor, each witness run on a JVM; a previous version that names a class only the new closure has is not verified; a declared change that throws on a null request compares that input; each refusal by name. Unit tests of the closure relocation, of the abstract methods accessors leave unread, and of the previous descriptor; the JBMC refusals in conformance.rs's pending test; a unit test of the route's command line for one closure, two and none. The default run passed, 34 of 34, before a last addition to the statement's words (the thrown declared change, only where a given implementation is among the inputs), after which the unit tests and the two interface test files were run again.

On the cached release JARs, inline, with the frozen allowed change, --nullable request, --gaps strict and --max-array-length 8: established in 0.1 s (0.8 s wall); refuted with no change declared (getMethod()="", run on a JVM).

Verification pending: job 20261115-181427-example-285-preservation-the-known-metho runs example 285's preservation task as stated (the gap packet's closure test, expected established), and job 20261115-181435-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c runs lib/tests/heap.rs's proof tier under JBMC at this commit, at low priority, since every regression check goes through the harness this changes. Example 285's three security jobs (20261115-173146-example-285-...) have passed, each as expected, and await collection; its sidecar keeps its blockers until the receipts are in the repository, and its notes say what is queued.

commits.summary: jvmcontract: under auto, JBMC is no fallback for a given implementation or a closure of the previous version's own
commits.body:
The regression check refused --engine jbmc and --confirm over a parameter given an implementation of its interface, and over a previous version on a dependency closure of its own (--before-classpath), but under --engine auto a run where the own checker had no verdict (out of time) would still have gone on to JBMC, which is given neither. It now stops there with a note, as it does for a String parameter: 'the tool's own checker gave no verdict, and JBMC is not asked: it takes an implementation of an interface the check gives, which only the own checker is given'. The assertions are in conformance.rs's test of the domains JBMC is not given (a looping method of the fixture, sourceTriangle, and a deadline of zero, for both cases); lib/tools' lint keeps a test that names JBMC out of the tool tier, which is why they are not in interface_regression.rs.

The second run of lib/tests/heap.rs's proof tier under JBMC, queued with the previous commit (20261115-181435-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c, about three hours), is withdrawn before it started: its job file is removed. It was to check that the regression harness is unchanged for inputs with no interface parameter and one class path. That is now shown directly: the 70 harness classes the heap tests' tool-tier proxies generate (57 regression, 13 property) are byte for byte the same at commit lvvpsuxl and at this one (a scratch build of that commit's lib/, sha256 of every harness class under target/tmp/heap*), and JBMC is running the proof tier on those bytes at lvvpsuxl (job 20261115-173209-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c). Withdrawing it also lets the pipeline collect example 285's preservation result (job 20261115-181427-example-285-preservation-the-known-metho, still pending) without waiting for three more hours of JBMC in the same run.

Verified by: the default run after the change passed 33 of 34, the one failure being the lint on where the new assertions first were (interface_regression.rs); after moving them, conformance.rs (10 passed, the changed test four times over), interface_regression.rs, interface_parameters.rs, values.rs, the unit tests and lib/tools' three lint suites were run again and pass.

commits.summary: Verification results for 6 jobs: example 285's four receipts pass, the conformance corpus passes, the object comparisons fail as in VF-018
commits.body: Ran 20261115-173146 (example 285 fixed, mutant, vulnerable: expected verdicts, outputs applied), 20261115-181427 (example 285 preservation, passed, outputs applied) and 20261115-173209-conformance (passed: JBMC and auto --confirm, 34m). 20261115-173209-object-comparisons (heap proof tier at 18cfa9e6) failed again on the same four tests as VF-018 (JBMC did not finish within 600 s), recorded there. 20261115-181435-object-comparisons was withdrawn by its submitter after it started and stopped; its leftover result was set aside, not collected (VF-029). Verified by pipeline.py status: nothing pending, running or uncollected.

commits.summary: Example 285 is decided: its four proof tasks have their receipts, each as expected, and its blockers are closed
commits.body:
Example 285 (CVE-2023-34055, Spring Boot's WebMvcTags.method(HttpServletRequest)) had every proof task refused before any proof (VF-027). With jvmcontract extended in the three commits before the pipeline's (lvvpsuxl, lustnxwm, oyvynrux), the unchanged claims were rerun on the released JARs by its own checker under strict gaps, and the pipeline collected the receipts in xkplwmyz: vulnerable-security refuted on 2.7.17 (witness request.getMethod() = "", the label ImmutableTag{key="method", value=""}, run on a JVM), fixed-security established on 2.7.18, mutant-security refuted on the mutant (the same witness), and preservation established between 2.7.17 and 2.7.18, each release on its own pinned closure. Each is as expected and not vacuous; the verifier's runs took 0.2 to 0.4 s.

This commit brings the example's records in line with the receipts. target.json lists no blocker (the four observed ones and the two predictions are removed) and its handoff says what is decided and what the claims leave open; each records/refusals/TASK.json keeps the refusal as it was observed and gains `closed`, naming the job and the receipt that decided the claim; example.json's summary, verdict label and notes say what was proved and about which domain (an implementation of HttpServletRequest that answers getMethod() with one non-null String of at most 8 code units, or a null request); the page's two blocker sections are replaced by 'The proofs' and 'Closed gaps'. The router and examples/gap-inventory.md are regenerated: 21 blocked obligations in five observed gaps, where there were 25; two-dependency-closures now blocks three tasks (286, 287 and 306's preservation, whose route no longer refuses them, so their rerun checks will fail as not predicted and their ordinary attempts will say what else each needs) and interface-parameter four (305's). VF-027 has a dated update saying so.

The tests that pinned the blocked state follow: test_gap_inventory.py's ranking, totals, dated predictions (285's two are gone) and closure tasks; test_workflow_refusal.py's table of blocked tasks (21), its rerun example (286's preservation, since 285's is decided), and a new test that a closed gap blocks nothing, predicts nothing, leaves the task executable and names a receipt that decided the unchanged claim as expected; test_acceptance.py accepts an earlier unresolved receipt of a task whose packet is closed. Verified by the Python half of the default run (32 of 33 suites, the one failure being the cost inventory's lint on the renamed tests, fixed with test_costs.py estimate and rerun with the three changed suites); nothing under lib/src or lib/tests changed since the last Rust run.

A correction to the previous commit's message (oyvynrux): it said the second heap proof-tier job, 20261115-181435-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c, was withdrawn before it started. The runner had started it at 18:25 UTC from the commit that queued it, before the commit that removed its job file landed; it was stopped, and its leftover result set aside (VF-029). The first one (20261115-173209-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c, at lvvpsuxl) failed on the four claims of VF-018, where JBMC does not finish in 600 s, as it did before these changes; its other five tests passed.
